title: Practice 7: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Tom ran away with the money.
exercises.why: **сбежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **сбежать** (to run down (from); to run away, to make off, to flee, to break out) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сбегать**. past: он сбежа́л · она сбежа́ла · оно сбежа́ло · они сбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «сбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вбежал** (**вбежать**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **забежал** (**забежать**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **прибежал** (**прибежать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A wasp flew into Tom's mouth.
exercises.why: **залетела** is the past tense (feminine) of **залететь** (to fly (in, into); to fly (as high as), to go up (as far as), to fly (as far as), to fly (behind, beyond)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **залетать**. past: он залете́л · она залете́ла · оно залете́ло · они залете́ли. — Wiktionary, «залететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **влетела** (**влететь**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **отлетела** (**отлететь**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **перелетела** (**перелететь**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **придёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. future: я приду́ · ты придёшь · он придёт · мы придём · вы придёте · они приду́т. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **выйдет** (**выйти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **дойдёт** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **подойдёт** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Where does the bus leave from?
exercises.why: **отходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **отходить** (to go away, to go aside, to move away, to move aside; (military) to withdraw, to fall back) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **отойти**. present: я отхожу́ · ты отхо́дишь · он отхо́дит · мы отхо́дим · вы отхо́дите · они отхо́дят. — Wiktionary, «отходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  Compare: «Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **выходит** (**выходить**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **обходит** (**обходить**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **переходит** (**переходить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: John came running into the room.
exercises.why: **вбежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **вбежать** (to come running in, to come rushing in, to run (into)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вбегать**. past: он вбежа́л · она вбежа́ла · оно вбежа́ло · они вбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «вбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **подбежал** (**подбежать**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **прибежал** (**прибежать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **убежал** (**убежать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A mouse came into the room.
exercises.why: **вбежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **вбежать** (to come running in, to come rushing in, to run (into)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вбегать**. past: он вбежа́л · она вбежа́ла · оно вбежа́ло · они вбежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «вбежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **забежала** (**забежать**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **подбежала** (**подбежать**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **убежала** (**убежать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **отвезу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **отвезти** (to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отвозить**. future: я отвезу́ · ты отвезёшь · он отвезёт · мы отвезём · вы отвезёте · они отвезу́т. — Wiktionary, «отвезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отвозить — отвезти — to take (haul) to отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёз деньги в банк.» (I took (by vehicle) money to the bank.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **вывезу** (**вывезти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **довезу** (**довезти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **провезу** (**провезти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **выйдем** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. future: я вы́йду · ты вы́йдешь · он вы́йдет · мы вы́йдем · вы вы́йдете · они вы́йдут. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33. exercises.q: He was taken off on a stretcher.
exercises.why: **унесли** is the past tense (plural) of **унести** (to take away, to take off, to carry (away); (figuratively) to take (a life), to claim (a life)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уносить**. past: он унёс · она унесла́ · оно унесло́ · они унесли́. — Wiktionary, «унести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «уносить — унести — to take (carry) away.» — DLI, Lesson 79. exercises.why: **заеду** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **заехать** (to call in on the way; to drive into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заезжать**. future: я зае́ду · ты зае́дешь · он зае́дет · мы зае́дем · вы зае́дете · они зае́дут. — Wiktionary, «заехать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **выеду** (**выехать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **приеду** (**приехать**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **проеду** (**проехать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **переплыли** is the past tense (plural) of **переплыть** (to swim across; to sail across) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переплывать**. past: он переплы́л · она переплыла́ · оно переплы́ло · они переплы́ли. — Wiktionary, «переплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination.
